sources.title: Gareth O. Roberts and Jeffrey S. Rosenthal, Coupling and Ergodicity of Adaptive MCMC
sources.locator: §2, adaptive-process setup, pp. 2–3; §5, Theorem 5 and proof, pp. 7–9; §6, Theorem 13 and proof, pp. 13–14; §7, Proposition 17 and Theorem 18, pp. 15–16; §9, Theorem 23 and Example 24, pp. 20–23.

contents.name: §2 common-invariant kernel family, adaptive filtration, and total-variation convention
contents.reason: The definition states the family, conditional transition rule, measurable adaptation size, and convergence in probability used by the local theorem.

contents.name: §6 convergence-time function and Theorem 13 (diminishing adaptation plus containment)
contents.reason: The convergence-time function and uniform-in-time bounded-in-probability condition are stated explicitly, including the fixed-initial-pair convention.

contents.name: Theorem 5 (simultaneous uniform ergodicity plus diminishing adaptation)
contents.reason: Both Theorem 5 and Theorem 13 are proved locally from the finite-block frozen-kernel perturbation bound.

contents.name: §7 Proposition 17 and Theorem 18 (common geometric drift and strongly aperiodic minorization imply containment)
contents.reason: A local split-coupling proof supplies constants uniform over the kernel family; the minorizing law is explicitly required to be supported on C as in the source's strongly aperiodic condition.

contents.name: Theorem 18 adaptive moment recursion followed by Theorem 13
contents.reason: The proof establishes a uniform V-moment bound, obtains containment by the local common geometric rate, and applies the preceding adaptive convergence theorem.

contents.name: Theorem 23 bounded-function weak law under Theorem 5 hypotheses
contents.reason: This pair proves marginal convergence and a strong-law counterexample; it does not add a separate weak-law theorem or its block-averaging proof.

contents.name: Example 24: diminishing adaptation does not guarantee a strong law, even under Theorem 5 conditions
contents.reason: A fully local finite-state construction establishes the same stronger conclusion: diminishing adaptation and simultaneous uniform ergodicity hold, while the bounded-function strong law fails almost surely along block endpoints. The paper’s adaptive One-Two construction is not imported.

contents.name: Theorem 19 polynomially ergodic families and later recurrence discussion
contents.reason: The controlling design selects only the uniform-ergodicity and containment convergence criteria and the geometric drift/minorization sufficient route.

sources.title: Gersende Fort, Adaptive MCMC: theory and methods, Warwick lecture notes
sources.locator: Slides 19–25: adaptive marginal convergence, diminishing adaptation, containment, and frozen-kernel comparison; slides 30–32: drift/minorization route to containment; complete 47-slide PDF retrieved.

contents.name: Slides 21–23: common-invariant adaptive marginal convergence from diminishing adaptation and containment
contents.reason: The notes give the convergence-time formulation and theorem conclusion; the local proof supplies the complete kernel-perturbation argument.

contents.name: Slide 25: frozen-chain decomposition of the adaptive marginal
contents.reason: The decomposition is made quantitative by a telescoping conditional-expectation proof with an explicit sum of adjacent total-variation changes.

contents.name: Slides 30–32: shared drift/minorization and bounded-in-probability convergence times
contents.reason: The local coupling lemma proves a common geometric convergence rate and the corollary converts the adaptive V-moment bound into containment.

contents.name: Slides 25–27: extension to parameter-dependent invariant distributions
contents.reason: The assigned page fixes one common invariant target for every kernel and does not claim convergence when the invariant laws vary with the parameter.

contents.name: Slides 34–40: Poisson-equation sufficient conditions for strong laws
contents.reason: No positive strong-law theorem is claimed; the assigned scope instead demonstrates that diminishing adaptation alone does not guarantee one.
